title: Practice: Food Chains and Food Webs

questions.stem: In a food web, grass is eaten by rabbits and grasshoppers. Rabbits are eaten by foxes. Grasshoppers are eaten by frogs, which are eaten by foxes. If a disease kills most of the frogs, what is the most likely short-term effect on the fox population?

options.text: The fox population would decline because frogs are their only food source
The fox population would be largely unaffected in the short term because foxes can still eat rabbits
The fox population would increase because there is less competition for rabbits
The fox population would immediately double

questions.explanation: In a food web, organisms typically have multiple food sources. Foxes eat both rabbits and frogs, so losing frogs does not eliminate their food supply. In the short term, foxes would rely more heavily on rabbits. However, increased predation on rabbits could eventually reduce the rabbit population, which might affect foxes later. Food webs show this interconnectedness.

questions.stem: In the food chain: Oak tree -> Caterpillar -> Blue tit -> Sparrowhawk, which organism is the secondary consumer?

options.text: Oak tree
Caterpillar
Blue tit
Sparrowhawk

questions.explanation: The oak tree is the producer (makes food by photosynthesis). The caterpillar is the primary consumer (eats the producer). The blue tit is the secondary consumer (eats the primary consumer). The sparrowhawk is the tertiary consumer (eats the secondary consumer). The trophic level is determined by position in the chain, not by whether the organism is a herbivore or carnivore.

questions.stem: A food web shows that mice eat seeds, and both owls and foxes eat mice. If the owl population suddenly decreases due to habitat loss, predict the likely effect on the mouse and fox populations.

options.text: Mouse population increases (less predation), which may lead to fox population increasing (more food available)
Mouse population decreases because foxes eat more mice to compensate
Fox population decreases because owls and foxes cooperate to hunt
No change occurs because owls and foxes are not connected in the food web

questions.explanation: With fewer owls, there is less predation pressure on mice, so the mouse population is likely to increase. With more mice available as prey, the fox population may then increase due to increased food supply. This demonstrates how removing one species from a food web can cause knock-on effects throughout the ecosystem.

questions.stem: All food chains begin with a producer. Why are producers essential for all food chains?

options.text: Producers are the largest organisms in the ecosystem
Producers convert light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis, providing the energy source that supports all other organisms in the food chain
Producers consume other organisms and pass the energy up the food chain
Producers release oxygen, which is the only thing consumers need

questions.explanation: Producers (mainly green plants and algae) carry out photosynthesis, converting light energy from the Sun into chemical energy stored in glucose. This is the entry point for energy into virtually all food chains. All consumers depend directly or indirectly on this energy. Without producers, there would be no energy input to sustain consumers at any trophic level.

questions.stem: A student states: 'A food web is more useful than a food chain for understanding an ecosystem.' Why is this correct?

options.text: Food webs are simpler and easier to draw than food chains
Food webs show only one feeding pathway, making predictions easier
Food webs show the interconnected feeding relationships between many species, giving a more realistic picture of how changes to one species affect others
Food webs include abiotic factors, while food chains do not

questions.explanation: A food chain shows only a single linear feeding pathway, which oversimplifies reality. A food web shows multiple interconnected food chains, revealing that most organisms eat and are eaten by several species. This complexity makes food webs better for predicting how changes (like the removal of a species) will affect the wider ecosystem.
